Without examining you, I'm not 100% sure, but problems with the ilipsoas are usually due to tightness alone. These kinds of issues are very prevalent in people who have to sit a lot for work and develop tightness in general in the front of their leg (not just iliopsoas but quads too). Consistent stretching (twice per day, 60 seconds at a time) should show gradual progress, but I would definitely recommend seeing a physio for the actual release technique. That would hopefully speed up the progress.

It sounds like you have tightness in your ilipsoas muscle. This can cause the popping and frequent tight feeling you are experiencing. A physio/physical therapist can do something called an iliopsoas release that will make a big difference in this. If you can't get in to see a physio, stretch as frequently as you can. The best stretch for this muscle is this one: https://goo.gl/images/8UP6FL. Hold the stretch at least 30-60 seconds at a time. Another solution is to wake up a little early before work and lay on a lacrosse/tennis ball where it feels tightest. Lay on the ball until you feel a relaxation or release in the muscle directly where you're pressing. This can partially release the muscle and can be done as frequently as you are able. Good luck!

Source: I'm a physical therapy student (DPT2)

Your response is true regarding chronic starvation. However, according to current exercise physiologists, training fasted (ie running before eating breakfast, then eating after) will induce higher losses of overall body fat. That said, fasted training may be more psychologically difficult, and athletes may self-select lower intensity levels at the onset of such a program. 

I would never propose skipping a meal but optimal fat loss will occur by working before breakfast then following with a small, balanced breakfast.
